summary.text: 叫 is traditionally analyzed as a compound: 口 marks a mouth-related meaning, while 丩 serves as a sound element. It is attested for shouting or calling, as well as animal cries and summoning; the order in which these uses arose is undated.

formation.text: 叫 is a phonosemantic compound. In its transmitted small-seal form, 口 stands on the left and 丩 on the right; the former contributes the mouth-related category and the latter is traditionally identified as the phonetic element. The surviving image is a modern redraw, not a securely dated artifact.

components.text: 口 contributes the mouth-related category associated with shouting or calling. It appears on the left in the transmitted small-seal form.
丩 is the right-hand component, traditionally identified as the phonetic element. Current and reconstructed readings offer comparisons, but do not settle the precise historical sound development.

sound_limitation.text: The historical comparisons depend on reconstruction system and do not resolve the precise sound development: Baxter–Sagart gives distinct forms, while the reported Zhengzhang forms share some sound material.

sound.text: In Baxter–Sagart Middle Chinese, 丩 and 叫 differ in initial and final; this comparison alone does not explain their historical relation.
The Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese forms share an initial but differ in other material; this comparison alone does not explain the phonetic development.
A reported Zhengzhang comparison gives 丩 *kɯw or *krɯw and 叫 *kiːws. The forms share *k- and w-related material but are not identical.
The Taiwan MOE Pinyin readings 丩 jiū and 叫 jiào are similar, but this modern comparison does not establish their historical sound relation.

history.text: The transmitted small-seal form is shown in a modern digital redraw. The available account gives neither the graph’s earliest attestation nor a continuous sequence of graphic changes.
No specific graphic corruption or other change to the character is established.

uncertainties.text: The traditional component analysis is documented, but the graph’s earliest appearance and the precise historical sound relation between 丩 and 叫 remain unresolved.
The cited early textual use has no precise date here. Other uses are attested, but the examples do not provide a dated sequence linking them.

senses.text: A cited Shijing phrase uses 叫 in an expression of shouting or calling; the date of this attestation is unresolved.

limitations.text: The examples attest distinct uses but do not establish their dates or semantic transitions, so no sequence of development is asserted.

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 釋義; 古籍例證
evidence.text: The dictionary records the Shuowen explanation for 叫 as “謼也。从口，丩聲” (to call/shout; from 口, with 丩 as phonetic), with 古弔切. The sources establish the traditional component analysis and attest early calling/shouting use; they do not date or document every later semantic extension.

context.provenance: Base evidence consists of imported local JSONL excerpts. Source names identify upstream datasets; extraction may lose sense and language boundaries. Further external evidence and research activity are documented separately in the dossier.
editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

search_audit.query: site:dict.variants.moe.edu.tw/dictView.jsp educode=C00010 丩 教育部 字典 Pinyin 丩 叫
search_audit.outcome: Performed one web search for the exact Taiwan MOE entries. Opened the requested 丩 and 叫 URLs; verified Pinyin jiū and jiào, and that 叫 repeats the traditional 从口，丩聲 analysis.

gaps: No visually inspected ancient glyph sequence for 叫 was obtained. The accessible Ministry dictionary indicates early-form resources (including oracle-bone and bronze references) are unavailable; the Han Dian graphic entry exposes category links but not a textual sequence. Earliest graphic attestation, graphic changes, and any proposed corruption remain undetermined.

The traditional Shuowen and Ministry dictionary analysis supports 口 as semantic and 丩 as phonetic, but evidence accessed here does not establish when the compound graph first appeared or independently demonstrate the precise historical phonetic derivation.

Early semantic evidence includes the 《詩經·小雅·北山》 phrase “或不知叫號,” preserved by the Ministry dictionary. No independently inspected dated manuscript or textual witness was found, so this research does not assign a precise date to that attestation. Later senses are documented as dictionary examples, but their chronological transitions are not established.

The early sound relationship remains system-dependent: checked Baxter–Sagart forms differ in final and morphology (*kˤewk-s for 叫 versus *k-riw for 丩), while the reported Zhengzhang forms share *kiːw- material. Do not merge these reconstructions or infer an identical pronunciation from the phonetic designation.

Official Unicode per-character Unihan pages for U+53EB and U+4E29 failed to load. Therefore modern kMandarin is not asserted as externally verified here, and no official per-character click-through evidence is available. The local full Unihan readings file was unavailable and the HSK extract had no matching entries.

Search result snippets and secondary summaries mention ancient forms and phonetic-series membership but were not treated as direct visual or primary paleographic inspection. No conflicting Shuowen account for 叫 was located; absence of one in this search does not establish that none exists.

The accessed sources support 口 as the semantic element and 丩 as the phonetic element by the traditional Shuowen analysis; no direct palaeographic evidence was inspected here for the compound’s earliest form, and the historical sound comparison needed to explain the precise phonetic development remains unresolved in this run.

The Shijing phrase is cited as early usage, but no dated manuscript witness was inspected; the date of the text’s composition and the date of surviving witnesses are not established by the pages checked. Later extensions to animal cry, summoning, naming, causative and passive uses are separately exemplified, but their transitions are not chronologically established.
No conflicting account of 叫’s formation was found in the inspected sources. No evidence for graphic corruption was found; this absence is not evidence that corruption is impossible.
A Xiaoxuetang search landing page and its rights notice were accessible, but no exact 叫 result record or image was retrieved; therefore no image from its interface is proposed.
The requested Unihan file contains no kMandarin rows for either character, so it cannot independently confirm their current Mandarin readings. The MOE entries provide the readings cited above.
This check concerns current readings only; it does not assess or modify Middle Chinese or Old Chinese reconstructions.

items.period: Shuowen small-seal tradition; transmitted lexicographic form, not a securely dated artifact
items.tradition: Small seal script, modern digital redraw
items.caption: In the Shuowen small-seal form of 叫, 口 appears on the left and 丩 on the right. The traditional analysis treats 口 as the semantic element and 丩 as the phonetic element.
items.alt: Black-line rendering of 叫 in the Shuowen small-seal style, with a box-like component on the left and a looping, angular component on the right.
items.selection_reason: This legible form illustrates the component layout described in the traditional analysis. It represents a transmitted small-seal form, not a securely dated artifact.
items.rights: Public domain release stated on the Commons file page; modern Inkscape vector redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph.

limitations.text: This modern redraw shows a Shuowen small-seal form; it does not establish the graph’s earliest attestation or a continuous history of graphic change.
